decisions.reason: F3 cited only the Dirac set-function definition although its probability property is proved in prop-dirac-measure-is-a-probability-measure. Added that existing choice-free supplier. Point-mass addition and two-sided scaling give necessity; convexity and the assumed vanishing give sufficiency, including zero and infinite-energy competitors. The Statement is unchanged.

The local strong-measurability definition requires a measure and allows a measure-dependent exceptional null set. On the bare measurable space the original hypothesis did not ensure integrability for arbitrary Jordan parts or lifts. Specified a single sequence of measurable simple functions converging at every point; boundedness and the Bochner criterion now give every signed moment, and the weighted feature has integrable norm. Variation domination and the explicit Jordan-sign lift prove the unchanged infimum and attainment claims.

The norm-convergence supplier requires a nonempty closed Euclidean domain, whereas the Statement admits the empty domain. Added the direct zero-measure argument for empty Theta before invoking F4 on nonempty Theta, and made the penalty counterexample explicitly use a nonempty domain. Compact-sphere finite-net approximation and scalar pairing prove the other claims; no Statement change or claim weakening.

The supplied definition of h2 starts at d>=2, so the original unrestricted first clause used an undefined local interface at d=1. Restored that declared dimensional premise only to the spherical clause; the partial clause is unchanged. The coupling proof bounds linear tails and quadratic tails by the fixed marginal and vanishing displacement, which proves both convergence assertions under AC. This does not discard any case in the supplied h2 definition.

The original h2 premise omitted the d>=2 domain of both projection suppliers. Added their dimensional premise and restated A1 as the explicit AC assumption. Reviewed the local all-endpoint energy derivation: superposition, quadratic feature growth and integrable action justify Fubini/FTC; radial subgradient scaling gives 4 integral(Gt squared) <= action. Uniform potential convergence and finite total action force the limiting square integral to vanish. No conclusion was weakened within the defined projection interface.

The rejected inference is valid: B(0,ra) is open and disjoint from A, so each point in that ball has a neighborhood disjoint from A and is outside closure(A), hence outside boundary(A). The prior path argument proves C_infinity misses this ball. Extra K points inside it cannot belong to boundary(C_infinity). Thus every boundary point has radius at least ra, the lower radial estimate keeps the small target outside its homotopy image, and degree zero near zero contrasts with degree one on the outer sphere. Characteristic pushforward and compactness justify the final support separation. No repair.

A1 incorrectly presented the AC definition as a derivation from the construction. AC is already an explicit hypothesis; restated it as an assumption and aligned axiom_use. Under the inherited partial hypotheses, the unchanged h1 W2 clause supplies signed narrow convergence, the projected-limit theorem gives convergence to inf F, and partial-energy continuity identifies that limit with F(mu_infinity). The continuous separable-Hilbert feature also meets the clarified relaxed-objective interface. Statement unchanged.

A1 attributed an unsupported inheritance assertion to the AC definition despite the explicit AC hypothesis. Restated A1 as that assumption and aligned axiom_use. The full two-homogeneous parent hypotheses already include d>=2, so the corrected W2 supplier applies. Equal-mass normalization, including the zero-mass case, identifies the finite spherical limit; projection identities identify its energy with F(mu_infinity), proving the unchanged global-minimum conclusion.
